originality.rationale: The 2026 full-monoid theorem proves a permutation inverse matching, not the explicit order-two optimal low-rank pairings. The 2024 integer-ratio theorem covers only the even-n rank-two existence subclaim; that subclaim is not presented as original. The new claim is the all-n concrete formulas together with fixed-idempotent optimality and exact cycle enumerations. The 2019 larger-semigroup theorem does not restrict its involution to isotone maps. Historical equivalent results remain possible.
residual_risks: An earlier construction under a different phrase (such as strong inverse pairing or a Rees 0-matrix incidence pairing) could coincide with the explicit formulas.

The 2024 paper discusses stronger existence conditions not exhaustively classified in present work. The claim of novelty is limited to explicit formulas plus optimal fixed-point/cycle census, not the bare existence of an involution.
The 2015 repository full text was not inspected; its published abstract clearly discusses inverse subsemigroup covers, a different assertion.

value.rationale: This all-n construction addresses an explicitly motivated strengthening of a recently solved permutation-matching problem, supplies optimal idempotent-fixed involutions in the first nonconstant and first singular Green strata, and classifies their full two-cycle statistics. The sharp parity obstruction in the n=5 rank-three stratum demonstrates a genuine structural boundary; it is not simply a textbook computation or arbitrary parameter slice.
